coverage.note: The plug-in solar bill story is statewide policy and named no address in its own text; its "1155 Market" and "1532 Mount Diablo Boulevard" hits both came from the next-post and previous-post navigation furniture, not the article. 1532 Mount Diablo Boulevard is in Walnut Creek.

findings.description: Recorded so the hit is not read again. The Registry's account of STG Group buying eight floors of 1155 Market Street for roughly $8 million, a decade after the space was valued at $80 million. This is the same transaction The San Francisco Standard reported on 28 August 2026 and which this module already extracted.

citation.label: The Registry, “STG Group Buys Eight Floors of San Francisco’s 1155 Market for $8MM, a Decade After $80MM Peak,” 3 September 2026

publish.note: One event, one entry. This is the same sale as finding 2026-08-28b-0001 in news/items/sf-standard/2026-08-28b.json, which carries it; the second outlet does not earn the building a second entry. That finding is itself still pending, and for a reason this article does not change: 1155 Market Street is a commercial condominium, carried in EAS only as #PARCEL A through D across four active parcels, none of which is the building. The subdivision is the story here too — eight floors sold, three kept — so a second citation on the same blocked fact adds nothing. If the site ever settles how it documents a vertically subdivided building, this article is a second source for that entry.

resolution.method: sf-eas-addresses has 1155 MARKET ST but it does not join to one parcel. 1155 MARKET ST's coordinates fall in 4 active parcels (3702821, 3702823, 3702822, 3702820), which is what a condominium looks like in sf-parcels: one parcel per unit, none of them the building.
resolution.note: The address is a condominium today, and the directory contract in the root AGENTS.md defers those: each unit has its own parcel and none of them is the building the record names.
